Who published the first widely accepted:
1) The first widely accepted table arranged the known elements by atomic mass and left gaps for undiscovered ones.
2) That work was published by the Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.
Answer: Dmitri Mendeleev.
Why the others are wrong: Moseley improved the table later by using atomic number, but he did not publish the first widely accepted version.
How are the elements arranged in the mod:
1) Moseley showed that the number of protons is the true ordering property.
2) The modern table therefore lists elements by increasing atomic number.
Answer: In order of increasing atomic number.
Why the others are wrong: Increasing atomic mass was Mendeleev's rule, which the modern table replaced.
How many groups (vertical columns) are i:
1) Groups are the vertical columns.
2) The standard table numbers them 1 through 18.
Answer: 18.
Why the others are wrong: Seven is the number of periods (horizontal rows), not groups.
What did Henry Moseley discover that imp:
1) Moseley studied the X-ray frequencies of elements.
2) The frequencies matched the nuclear charge (atomic number), so atomic number is the correct ordering.
3) This fixed pairs such as Te and I that were out of order by mass.
Answer: The properties of elements follow atomic number, not atomic mass.
Why the others are wrong: The triad idea came earlier from Dobereiner, not from Moseley.
Which statement is the modern periodic l:
1) The periodic law links properties to the ordering of the elements.
2) The modern ordering is by atomic number, so properties repeat with atomic number.
Answer: Properties of elements repeat periodically when elements are arranged by atomic number.
Why the others are wrong: The mass version is the original Mendeleev statement, which is no longer used.
The s-block spans groups 1 and 2 and has:
1) Each period contributes the two elements of its s sublevel (2 electrons fill it).
2) Number of elements = 7 periods x 2 = 14.
Answer: 14.
Why the others are wrong: Seven counts only one element per period and ignores that the s sublevel holds two electrons.
Periods 1, 2 and 3 contain 2, 8 and 8 el:
1) Add the elements in each period.
2) 2 + 8 + 8 = 18 elements.
Answer: 18.
Why the others are wrong: Twenty-eight comes from wrongly counting 18 elements in period 3.
Mendeleev left a gap below silicon and p:
1) The gap sat in the same group as silicon, so the element had to be in group 14 below Si.
2) Germanium (Ge) is in group 14 with atomic mass 72.6.
3) It was discovered in 1886 and matched the predictions.
Answer: Germanium.
Why the others are wrong: Gallium also filled a Mendeleev gap, but it sits in group 13 below aluminum, not below silicon.
In a Dobereiner triad the middle element:
1) Average the outer two masses: (35.45 + 126.90) / 2.
2) 162.35 / 2 = 81.175, about 81.2 amu.
3) The real mass of Br is 79.9 amu, so the prediction is close.
Answer: About 81.2 amu.
Why the others are wrong: 91.5 is the difference of the masses, and 162.4 is their sum; neither is an average.
1) Periods 1 to 3 hold 2 + 8 + 8 = 18 elements, so period 4 starts at Z = 19 (group 1).
2) Group 17 is 16 places after group 1, so Z = 19 + 16 = 35.
3) This is bromine.
Answer: 35.
Why the others are wrong: 36 is group 18 (krypton), the element just after bromine.
What is the name of the family of elemen:
1) Group 1 contains Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs and Fr.
2) These soft, very reactive metals are called the alkali metals.
Answer: Alkali metals.
Why the others are wrong: Alkaline earth metals are in group 2, one column to the right.

1) Group 17 contains F, Cl, Br and I.
2) This reactive nonmetal family is called the halogens.
Answer: Halogens.
Why the others are wrong: Noble gases are in group 18, the column next to the halogens.
How many valence electrons does a neon a:
1) Neon is in group 18 (Z = 10), configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6.
2) Its outer level (n = 2) has 2 + 6 = 8 electrons.
Answer: 8.
Why the others are wrong: 10 is the total number of electrons, not just the valence electrons.
What does the period number of an elemen:
1) Elements in one row fill the same principal energy level.
2) So the period number equals the highest occupied energy level n.
Answer: The number of the outermost occupied energy level.
Why the others are wrong: The number of valence electrons is given by the group, not the period.
How many valence electrons does calcium:
1) Calcium is in group 2.
2) Main-group elements in group 2 have 2 valence electrons (4s2).
Answer: 2.
Why the others are wrong: 20 is calcium's atomic number, not its valence electron count.
Why do elements in the same group have s:
1) Chemical behavior depends on the valence electrons.
2) All members of a group have the same valence configuration, so they react in similar ways.
Answer: They have the same number of valence electrons.
Why the others are wrong: Atoms in a group have different numbers of protons and different numbers of energy levels.
Calcium (group 2) combines with chlorine:
1) Ca loses 2 electrons to form Ca2+, and Cl gains 1 electron to form Cl-.
2) One Ca2+ needs two Cl- to balance charge.
3) The formula is CaCl2.
Answer: CaCl2.
Why the others are wrong: CaCl would give a net charge of +1, so the charges do not cancel.
In the reaction 2Na + Cl2 -> 2NaCl, how:
1) The balanced equation shows 2 mol Na per 1 mol Cl2.
2) Moles of Cl2 = 6.0 mol x (1 / 2) = 3.0 mol.
Answer: 3.0 mol.
Why the others are wrong: 6.0 mol assumes a 1 to 1 ratio, which ignores the coefficient 2 on Na.
Aluminum (group 13) reacts with oxygen (:
1) Aluminum loses 3 electrons to form Al3+. Oxygen gains 2 electrons to form O2-.
2) The lowest common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6, so use 2 Al (+6) and 3 O (-6).
3) The formula is Al2O3.
Answer: Al2O3.
Why the others are wrong: Al3O2 swaps the charges onto the wrong atoms: it gives +9 and -4.
An atom has 2 occupied energy levels and:
1) Two occupied levels means period 2.
2) Seven valence electrons means group 17.
3) Total electrons = 2 + 7 = 9, so Z = 9, which is fluorine.
Answer: Fluorine, group 17.
Why the others are wrong: Chlorine has 3 energy levels (period 3), and group 7 is not a group number in the 1 to 18 system.
Moving from left to right across a perio:
1) Across a period the nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same energy level.
2) The stronger pull draws the electrons in, so the radius decreases.
Answer: It generally decreases.
Why the others are wrong: Adding electrons does not make the atom larger when they go into the same energy level.
Moving down a group, what happens to ato:
1) Each period down adds a new energy level.
2) Electrons in a higher level are farther from the nucleus, so the radius increases.
Answer: It increases.
Why the others are wrong: The nuclear charge also grows, but extra energy levels and shielding outweigh it.
Which atom has the largest atomic radius:
1) F, Cl, Br and I are in the same group.
2) Radius increases down a group and iodine is lowest, so iodine is largest.
Answer: Iodine.
Why the others are wrong: Fluorine is the smallest, not the largest, of the halogens.
Why does atomic radius decrease across a:
1) Moving right adds one proton and one electron per element.
2) The new electron goes in the same level and shields little, so the effective nuclear charge rises.
3) The electron cloud is pulled closer.
Answer: The nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same energy level.
Why the others are wrong: Adding energy levels happens down a group, not across a period.
Which list shows the atoms in order of i:
1) Na, Mg, P and Cl are all in period 3.
2) Radius decreases left to right, so Na is largest and Cl smallest.
3) Increasing order is Cl, P, Mg, Na.
Answer: Cl, P, Mg, Na.
Why the others are wrong: Na, Mg, P, Cl is the decreasing order, which is the reverse of what was asked.
The radius of a chlorine atom is 99 pm a:
1) Ratio = ion radius / atom radius.
2) 181 pm / 99 pm = 1.83.
3) The ion is larger because the added electron repels the others while the nuclear charge stays the same.
Answer: 1.83 times.
Why the others are wrong: 0.55 comes from dividing the atom radius by the ion radius, the inverse ratio.
The atomic radius of sodium is 186 pm an:
1) Find the difference in radii.
2) 186 pm - 99 pm = 87 pm.
Answer: 87 pm.
Why the others are wrong: 285 pm adds the two radii instead of subtracting them.
Which species has the smallest radius: O:
1) All four have 10 electrons, so they are isoelectronic.
2) With the same electrons, more protons pull harder: O 8, F 9, Na 11, Mg 12 protons.
3) Mg2+ has the most protons, so it is the smallest.
Answer: Mg2+.
Why the others are wrong: O2- has the fewest protons for its 10 electrons, so it is the largest, not the smallest.
A sodium atom has a radius of 186 pm. If:
1) Diameter = 2 x 186 pm = 372 pm = 3.72 x 10^-10 m.
2) Length 1.00 mm = 1.00 x 10^-3 m.
3) Number = 1.00 x 10^-3 / 3.72 x 10^-10 = 2.69 x 10^6.
Answer: 2.69 x 10^6.
Why the others are wrong: 5.38 x 10^6 uses the radius instead of the diameter.
Potassium has more protons than sodium,:
1) Na has 3 energy levels and K has 4.
2) The outer electron of K is in n = 4, farther from the nucleus.
3) Inner electrons shield it, so the added distance outweighs the extra protons.
Answer: Potassium has an extra energy level, and inner electrons shield the outer electron.
Why the others are wrong: Potassium has more protons and more electrons than sodium, not fewer.
What is first ionization energy?\nThe en:
1) Ionization means removing an electron from a neutral atom in the gas phase.
2) The first ionization energy is the energy needed for the outermost electron.
Answer: The energy needed to remove the outermost electron from a gaseous atom.
Why the others are wrong: Energy released on gaining an electron is the electron affinity, not ionization energy.
Which element has the highest electroneg:
1) Electronegativity rises toward the upper right of the table (ignoring noble gases).
2) Fluorine has the highest value, 4.0 on the Pauling scale.
Answer: Fluorine.
Why the others are wrong: Francium is at the opposite corner and has one of the lowest values.
How does first ionization energy change:
1) Lower in a group, the outer electron is in a higher energy level.
2) It is farther from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is easier to remove and the energy decreases.
Answer: It generally decreases.
Why the others are wrong: Increase is the trend across a period, not down a group.
Which element has the lowest first ioniz:
1) K and Na are in group 1, Mg and Al are further right in period 3.
2) Ionization energy decreases down a group and increases across a period.
3) K is lowest, 419 kJ/mol compared with Na at 496 kJ/mol.
Answer: K.
Why the others are wrong: Na is low, but K is below it in the same group and so is even lower.
How does electronegativity generally cha:
1) Across a period the effective nuclear charge rises and the radius shrinks.
2) Atoms then attract bonding electrons more strongly, so electronegativity increases.
Answer: It increases.
Why the others are wrong: A larger radius would lower the pull, but the radius shrinks across a period.
The electronegativity of Na is 0.9 and o:
1) Difference = 3.0 - 0.9 = 2.1.
2) Since 2.1 is greater than 1.7, electrons are transferred.
3) The bond is ionic.
Answer: Ionic.
Why the others are wrong: Polar covalent applies to a difference of about 0.5 to 1.7, and 2.1 is above that.
The first and second ionization energies:
1) Removing two electrons needs both steps.
2) Total = 738 kJ + 1451 kJ = 2189 kJ.
Answer: 2189 kJ.
Why the others are wrong: 713 kJ is the difference between the two values, not their sum.
The first ionization energy of sodium is:
1) Energy = moles x ionization energy per mole.
2) 2.50 mol x 496 kJ/mol = 1240 kJ.
Answer: 1240 kJ.
Why the others are wrong: 198 kJ comes from dividing 496 by 2.50 instead of multiplying.
Magnesium has ionization energies of 738:
1) The jump from 1451 to 7733 is more than fivefold.
2) A big jump occurs when removal starts from an inner full level.
3) So Mg has two valence electrons (3s2), consistent with group 2.
Answer: Magnesium has 2 valence electrons, and the third electron comes from an inner, closer level.
Why the others are wrong: If Mg had 3 valence electrons the large jump would appear after the third value, not before it.
The first ionization energy of sodium is:
1) Convert 496 kJ to J: 496 x 1000 = 4.96 x 10^5 J per mol.
2) Divide by atoms per mole: 4.96 x 10^5 / 6.022 x 10^23.
3) This equals 8.24 x 10^-19 J per atom.
Answer: 8.24 x 10^-19 J.
Why the others are wrong: 8.24 x 10^-22 J forgets to convert kJ to J.
Which property is typical of metals?\nTh:
1) Metals have mobile valence electrons.
2) These electrons carry charge and heat, so metals are good conductors.
Answer: They conduct electricity well.
Why the others are wrong: Brittleness and poor conduction describe nonmetals, not metals.
Which of these elements is a metalloid?\:
1) Metalloids lie along the staircase line and include B, Si, Ge, As, Sb and Te.
2) Silicon is in this list.
Answer: Silicon.
Why the others are wrong: Aluminum sits next to the staircase, but it is a metal.
Which of these elements is a liquid at r:
1) Only two elements are liquid at room temperature: mercury and bromine.
2) Bromine is the nonmetal of the two.
Answer: Bromine.
Why the others are wrong: Iodine is a halogen too, but it is a solid at room temperature.
A solid shatters when struck with a hamm:
1) Metals are malleable and conduct, so they do not shatter or insulate.
2) Brittle, dull and nonconducting are nonmetal properties.
Answer: A nonmetal.
Why the others are wrong: Metals bend or flatten when struck, they do not shatter.
Brass is an alloy that is 70.0 percent c:
1) Mass of copper = percentage x total mass.
2) 0.700 x 250 g = 175 g.
Answer: 175 g.
Why the others are wrong: 75 g is the zinc portion (30.0 percent), not the copper.
What is the mass of 0.500 mol of silicon:
1) Mass = moles x molar mass.
2) 0.500 mol x 28.09 g/mol = 14.0 g.
Answer: 14.0 g.
Why the others are wrong: 56.2 g comes from dividing by 0.500 instead of multiplying.
Copper has a density of 8.96 g/cm^3. Wha:
1) Mass = density x volume.
2) 8.96 g/cm^3 x 25.0 cm^3 = 224 g.
Answer: 224 g.
Why the others are wrong: 2.79 g comes from dividing volume by density, which gives the wrong units.
Magnesium reacts with oxygen to form MgO:
1) Each Mg atom loses 2 electrons to form Mg2+, and oxygen gains them.
2) Electrons = 3.0 mol Mg x 2 = 6.0 mol.
Answer: 6.0 mol.
Why the others are wrong: 3.0 mol counts only one electron per magnesium atom.
Which pair correctly describes the usual:
1) A metal oxide such as Na2O reacts with water to form a base (NaOH).
2) A nonmetal oxide such as SO2 or CO2 reacts with water to form an acid.
3) So metal oxides are basic and nonmetal oxides acidic.
Answer: Metal oxides are basic and nonmetal oxides are acidic.
Why the others are wrong: The reversed pairing reflects mixing up which side of the staircase is which.
An element is shiny but brittle, conduct:
1) Shiny suggests a metal, but brittle and weakly conducting do not fit.
2) Conductivity that rises with temperature is semiconductor behavior.
3) This mix, with the position on the staircase, identifies a metalloid.
Answer: A metalloid.
Why the others are wrong: A metal would be malleable and conduct strongly, and a nonmetal would be dull.
